record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a refusal-direction projection implemented as a per-request LoRA adapter and evaluates its behavioral effect. This is a practical weight-delta implementation, but it is not the original all-layer, all-position residual-stream intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports an outcome for the rank-1 adapter on one model. The suggested zero-adapter comparison and soak test have no reported results. Direction-artifact similarity values are discussed for choosing a basis, not reported as tests of the claim.
record.test_reason: The repo applies a published abliteration direction as an exact LoRA weight delta on a released model, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017. It reports refusal rates with and without it, a new deployment setting for V2. It does not say how the direction was derived, so it cannot confirm that a difference-in-means direction is what mediates refusal (V1).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The README argues that the weight edit and the LoRA delta are exactly the same operation (identity checked to 1e-9). On that basis the ablation can be applied per request and reversed without writing the checkpoint. Refusals fell from 98.5% to 2.5%, with injection resistance unchanged and a small decode cost. The authors explicitly say this is not a general claim about abliteration.
record.recipe_differences: The adapter implements the projection as a weight delta, but it uses an external rank-1 direction artifact and applies it only to attn.wo_b in layers 2–39. It does not report the original difference-in-means derivation or an all-layer, all-position residual-stream ablation. This is a tool repo; the README reports evaluation results.
record.method_sensitivity: The README warns that outcomes may depend on the direction artifact, engine and tensor-parallel layout, adapter routing, FP8 operation order and replay behavior. It reports results for only one basis and deployment.

fits_no_version.finding: With the adapter, caution markers on destructive-operation prompts stayed present in 18/20 (vs 20/20). In the two failures, the warning came only after agreeing to the action, where the base model refused first. Injection leaks stayed 0/22.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-direction ablation weakens refuse-first behaviour on agentic destructive operations while leaving prompt-injection resistance intact.

record.problems: README-only evidence; no code execution or independent verification. Results cover one model, one deployment and one adapter basis. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Harm-prompt replies are not stored, and the README says its caution metric is marker-based and can overstate preservation.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported outcome rows left out. The README's basis-similarity values are used to distinguish or choose direction artifacts, not reported as tests of refusal mediation. Suggested zero-adapter, comparison and soak checks have no outcome values.

untested.parts: Derivation of the direction is not stated (no difference-in-means shown). No test of adding the direction to induce refusal. Ablation covers only attn.wo_b in layers 2–39, not every layer and position. No broad capability evaluation.
Only one model, one deployment (FP8, TP=4) and one basis (pqhaz). The second public basis (mrfakename) is not evaluated. No permanently edited checkpoint is tested. No uncertainty is reported.

record.verdict_notes: This is a README-only tool repo with self-reported numbers and no stored harm replies. The decode throughput and TTFT numbers (70.1 vs 68.5 tok/s) are engineering costs, not results bearing on any version, so no rows are needed. The README notes that the two public bases have a median |cos| of 0.565. This means the choice of basis matters, but no outcome is reported for the second basis. A vLLM replay path may silently leave late layers unablated, a further method-sensitivity caveat.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not state how the direction was derived, does not test adding it to induce refusals, and applies the adapter only to attn.wo_b in layers 2–39 rather than ablating it at every layer and position. Its non-refusal evaluations are limited and do not establish broad capability retention.
Tests a per-request LoRA adapter equivalent to a weight delta, not a permanently edited released checkpoint; only one model, deployment and adapter basis are reported.
No reported test of attacks suppressing the refusal direction or training against its ablation.
No test of whether refusal requires an affine set, cone or multiple directions.
No test separating harmfulness judgment from refusal.
No transfer test across languages, model variants or base and instruct models.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or stages.

relation.reason: It reports its own base-vs-adapter refusal rates on 200 harm prompts, so its results bear on whether the weight-edit ablation removes refusal in a released model.

tranche.reason: It applies an existing abliteration direction as an exactly equivalent weight delta to a new released model and deployment setting (per-request LoRA, attn.wo_b only, FP8 TP=4), and it reports refusal rates with and without the delta. That is a result on V2 in a new setting. It is not T4, because the refusal rate it reports is the thing V2 claims.

source_check.notes: The pack gave no [lN] id for the V2 verdict, so label_id is 'none_in_pack'. Strength s=2.5 in W-s·qqᵀW overshoots a pure projection (s=1). The edit touches only attn.wo_b, not every residual writer. The direction's derivation, the refusal scorer and the serving engine for the Results are all unstated. The concern that vLLM replay layers may skip the adapter comes from reading code, not from a measurement.
